sequence_notes.rule: Every shot is built in layers. Veo animates the world with the camera locked; Premiere does every camera move, cut and grade; ffmpeg draws every piece of on-screen text, the HUD, the waveform, timestamps and the beacon pulses that must hit a word.
sequence_notes.why: Veo's worst failure (inventing new objects as the camera travels) is caused by camera movement, so locking it stops the bug. Premiere's API cannot write text at all. 'Veo' below means Flow's video model: Omni Flash by Jack's standing ruling, Veo 3.1 only where Omni cannot do the job. Never pin an end frame; chain last frame into first frame when a beat needs more than one clip.

sequence_notes.rule: The HUD changes are hard cuts, never dissolves, and red means kill mode only. Patrol = grey CCTV with the red HUD (#3). The signal = the waveform arrives over the SAME shot and the picture stops sweeping (#4). Then a hard cut with a sound jump: the muffled waveform audio becomes the full-volume row (#6). KILL MODE ENGAGED = a single-frame flip to full red (#8).
sequence_notes.why: A colour code works through rarity and consistency, so red must appear only when the machines are hunting. The waveform-to-row cut is the joke, and a hard cut makes the viewer join the two images. Sound leading the picture (a J-cut) makes two places feel like one thought. Run ffmpeg photosensitivity on the red flip and the explosions.
sequence_notes.source: docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/scenes/second-half-storyboard-plan.md (the HUD rule); docs/cinematography/principles.md principle 16; docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §3 (hard cut, J-cut); docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/restructure-2026-10-15.md beat C2; docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §5 (photosensitivity)

sequence_notes.rule: The look travels as a grade layer, not as different prompts. Bunker, meeting and street frames get one shared 16mm treatment (moving grain, slight gate weave, green shadows) in ffmpeg or Premiere. It switches off on ONE hard cut: the walk-in at #20. The old lady (#17) keeps her anamorphic look as the one exception. The clean room still gets fine moving grain.
sequence_notes.why: Kai ruled that the contrast between the bunker and the AI's building is the point, so it should land in one place, on a cut. A locked plate without moving grain reads as a frozen JPEG. Planning colour for the whole piece first is how we stop frames drifting apart.
sequence_notes.source: docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/restructure-2026-10-15.md round 5; docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/scenes/second-half-storyboard-plan.md look rule; docs/cinematography/principles.md principle 15; memory: hybrid-video-method (moving grain is not optional)

sequence_notes.rule: World motion is dramatic everywhere; camera motion is rationed. Make the things inside the frame move hard (tracks grinding, dust, explosions, beacons). Spend real camera movement on only two places: the kill-mode race (#8 to #10) and the ending zoom-out (#28 to #29). Elsewhere: locked, or one slow eased push that arrives at something.
sequence_notes.why: Kai asked for dramatic animation, not vague twinkle. The house rule is that a single camera move in a still body of work lands hard only if the stillness around it is real. These two rules fit together once you separate 'does the world move?' from 'does the camera move?'.
sequence_notes.source: memory: dramatic-video-animation (Kai, 2026-09-13); docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §1 (house ruling 2026-08-26, the motion economy); docs/story-craft/forms.md §5 (one moving shot per video); docs/cinematography/stills.md §5

sequence_notes.rule: The clean room runs wide to close and passes the visible-cost gate. Order: #20 wide arrival, #22 hall, #23 wafer, #24 overhead pattern, #25 floor level with faces, #26 mud on white, #27 empty chairs. Every monumental frame (#20, #22, #23, #24) either carries a cost in frame (mud, worn jumpers, a small human) or sits next to one. The near-black/monumental register question (R1) is still OPEN; nothing here settles it.
sequence_notes.why: A fixed shot-size direction reads as moving toward the truth; random jumps read as chaos. Scale and symmetry with no cost in frame read as celebrating the power. Satire of power does not protect you. The overhead is only an establisher: it shows pattern and spends the people, so the floor-level shot must follow it.
sequence_notes.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §2 step 3; docs/cinematography/principles.md gate 2, principles 21a, 23, 24, §R1; docs/cinematography/registers.md §1 (the gate)

sequence_notes.rule: Design out what the engine cannot do before spending a credit. No four-or-more walkers (#19, #20), no balance poses (#21's hopping man), no two speakers in one clip (#7), no 'reach a state' moments (a seat slamming down, a beacon switching off), and no camera travel past rows of identical things (houses, chairs, ceiling panels). Count 1 per roll. Kai approves every still before any video credit. Picture is cut first; the narration fits after, so all seconds here are estimates.
sequence_notes.why: Every clip Jack called 'AI slop' on The Bank Robbery asked for one of these. A camera passing repeated objects makes Veo regenerate them. Two takes on a locked plate come back nearly identical, so a second candidate wastes credits.
sequence_notes.source: docs/google-flow/README.md (what the video model cannot do); docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §2b, §7; memory: flow-video-count-one; docs/cinematography/stills.md §6 (still-approval gate)

frames.job: Establish the place and the threat in one wide: five years on, the machines own the streets.

options.label: Locked aerial, slow push
options.idea: The machines keep circling the ring in the locked frame. Premiere adds a slow eased push that lands on one machine, the one we meet low down in #2.

lanes.does: Three machines track slowly round the ring; dust lifts behind them.
Hold 1s, then an eased push of about 10% toward one machine.
16mm-free grade check, moving grain.

options.veo_prompt: High aerial, the camera does not move. The three tracked machines keep rolling slowly round the roundabout on patrol, one behind another; grey dust lifts behind their tracks. The abandoned cars and weeds stay still. Muted dusk light. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: hard cut from the bot scene (the robot trundles off). Out: cut on the machine the push arrives at, into #2.
options.risk: Small far-off movers can blur together; three movers is under the four-mover limit.
options.source: docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §2; docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §2 step 2 (geography once, early); docs/cinematography/principles.md principle 21a (a high wide is an establisher)

options.label: Veo descending arc
options.idea: Let Veo move the camera: a slow descending arc over the junction. Aerials with no glass grid are where Veo may move the camera.

lanes.does: A slow descent with no more than 35-40 degrees of arc.
Trim to the clean seconds; grade.

options.veo_prompt: Slow descending aerial arc over the roundabout, turning no more than a quarter turn. The tracked machines keep circling the ring below, dust lifting. Every car and building keeps its exact shape.
options.cut: In: hard cut. Out: cut while the camera is still moving, into the low shot #2.
options.risk: Abandoned cars are repeated objects and may change as the camera moves; arcs over about 40 degrees redesign objects.
options.source: memory: dramatic-video-animation (Kai, 2026-09-13); docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §7 (orbit limit)

options.label: Intercut with their eyes
options.idea: Use the still with only grain and a light shake, cut short and alternated with the POV #3, as Kai suggested for the patrol (their eyes and the roundabout, intercut).

lanes.does: Held plate with Camera Shake at about 10 so it reads as filmed.
Moving grain.

options.cut: In: hard cut. Out: alternates with #3 two or three times.
options.risk: Without motion the still can read as a photograph if held longer than 2s.
options.source: docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/restructure-2026-10-15.md round 5; docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §2 table (no/no row); docs/cinematography/stills.md §4

recommended.why: It establishes the geography once, gives the world real motion, and the push hands a specific machine to #2.

frames.job: Make the machine huge and close: the menace, at our height.

options.label: It rolls at the lens
options.idea: Locked low camera in the gutter; the machine keeps rolling toward the lens, tracks grinding, leaves and dust lifting. Premiere adds a rumble shake that grows as it nears.

lanes.does: The machine advances, tracks turning, debris lifting.
Camera Shake keyed to grow as it nears; cut before it fills the frame.
Grain.

options.veo_prompt: Low in the gutter, the camera does not move. The tracked machine keeps rolling heavily toward camera, its tracks grinding over grit, dead leaves and dust kicked up and swirling around them. Its box sensor turns slowly. Teal shadows, warm haze. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: from the machine the aerial push found. Out: cut on movement as the sensor turns to camera, into its own view (#3).
options.risk: Track links can smear; keep the machine moving at a steady pace, not stopping or turning.
options.source: docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §3 (force verbs: grind, kick); docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §3 (cut on movement); docs/cinematography/principles.md gate 2 (the ruined street is the cost)

options.label: The sensor finds us
options.idea: Only the sensor moves: the box turns and stops, pointing straight down the lens. A held, still threat, then cut into what it sees.

lanes.does: Only the sensor turns; machine stationary.
A tiny push of 3-4% as the sensor arrives.

options.veo_prompt: Low in the gutter, the camera does not move. The machine is stopped. Only its box-shaped sensor turns slowly on the turret until it points straight at the camera, then holds. Dust settles round the tracks. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: hard cut. Out: the sensor's stare cuts to its POV (#3), a clean match.
options.risk: A turning part can 'reach' a final position badly; it may overshoot or wobble.
options.source: docs/cinematography/stills.md §1 (an unresolved question: it is looking at something); docs/google-flow/README.md (what the video model cannot do) (continue a state)

options.label: Rolls over the lens
options.idea: The machine rolls right over the camera; its belly blacks the frame and that black is the cut into its POV.

lanes.does: The machine advances until its body covers the lens.
Use the black frames as the cut point into #3.

options.veo_prompt: Low in the gutter, the camera does not move. The tracked machine rolls straight over the camera, its dark underside sliding across the whole frame until it is black. Dust and leaves swirl. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: hard cut. Out: black frame to #3.
options.risk: High: 'arriving' over the lens is reaching a state, which the engine does badly; it may stop short or morph.
options.source: docs/google-flow/README.md (what the video model cannot do); docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §5 (a strong graphic anchor carries a cut)

recommended.why: Most dramatic with the lowest risk; the turning sensor still gives a clean match into the POV.

frames.job: Put us inside the hunter's eyes and teach the HUD before it changes.

options.label: Post push + HUD
options.idea: No credit spent: a slow forward push on the CCTV plate, which is low-res and noisy enough to hide that it is a still, plus the full patrol HUD.

lanes.does: Slow forward push with a slight fisheye; tiny lateral sway like a tracked vehicle.
Red patrol HUD (drawtext + drawbox): ticking range and heading values, scanlines, video noise.

options.cut: In: on the sensor turn from #2. Out: continues straight into #4 (same shot).
options.risk: A 2D push has no parallax; the CCTV degradation must be heavy enough to hide it.
options.source: docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §6c (flat or degraded subject = post); docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §5 (text only in ffmpeg); docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/scenes/second-half-storyboard-plan.md HUD rule

options.label: Living street, sensor sweep
options.idea: Veo animates small life in the locked street (a plastic bag blowing, weeds stirring, a loose gutter swinging). Premiere does the sensor's slow side-to-side sweep. HUD on top.

lanes.does: Wind life in the street.
Slow pan left then right: the sensor scanning.
Patrol HUD with a moving bearing scale that tracks the pan.

options.veo_prompt: Grainy security-camera view, the camera does not move. A gust pushes a plastic bag tumbling along the road; weeds and a broken gutter sway in the wind. Nothing else moves. Keep the low-resolution video noise. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: on the sensor turn. Out: the sweep STOPS on the cut into #4.
options.risk: Fine particulate over dark detail doesn't animate; ask for big things like the bag and gutter.
options.source: docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §2 (yes/yes = the hybrid); docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §6b (Veo animates what the plate gives it)

options.label: Veo creeps forward
options.idea: Let Veo roll the camera forward down the street for real parallax, and cut before the houses start to regenerate.

lanes.does: Slow forward roll at 70cm height.
HUD; trim to the first 3s.

options.veo_prompt: Security-camera view rolling slowly forward down the empty street at knee height. The abandoned cars and houses keep their exact shape. Keep the low-resolution video noise.
options.cut: In: on the sensor turn. Out: cut at 3s into #4.
options.risk: High: terraced houses and parked cars are rows of near-identical objects; expect regeneration after 3-4s.
options.source: docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §2b; memory: dramatic-video-animation (Kai, 2026-09-13) (let Veo move and cut before it breaks)

recommended.why: Real life in the frame plus a sensor sweep that can STOP on the ping: the stop is the signal.

frames.job: The turn: the machine hears us. Set up the joke with a sound we can't make out.

options.label: Same shot, sweep stops
options.idea: Continue #3 without a cut. On the first ping the sweep freezes and the waveform band draws itself across the frame, two voices tagged. Muffled argument underneath.

lanes.does: The pan stops dead on ping 1.
Waveform band and the two voice tags drawn in time with the pings; ORGANIC SIGNAL DETECTED type-on.

options.cut: In: no cut from #3. Out: hard cut with a sound jump; the muffled audio becomes the full row (#5 or #6).
options.risk: Little; the risk is holding too long. Kai said brief.
options.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §2 step 5 (set a pattern, then break it); docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/scenes/second-half-storyboard-plan.md HUD rule; docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §5

options.label: Digital enhance
options.idea: On each ping, Premiere steps the scale up hard (100, 115, 130) like a camera zooming on a sound, the noise getting coarser. Waveform on top.

lanes.does: Three hard scale steps on the pings, no easing.
Waveform, tags, coarser pixelation per step.

options.cut: In: cut from #3. Out: hard cut to the row.
options.risk: Can look like a TV-thriller 'enhance' cliché if the steps are not on the pings.
options.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §1 (what does the move mean that stillness would not?)

options.label: Turn toward the sound
options.idea: The sensor swings quickly toward the source: a fast post pan that settles on the open downs, while the waveform grows. It points where the bunker is.

lanes.does: One fast eased pan, settling.
Waveform and a bearing marker locking on.

options.cut: In: from #3. Out: hard cut to the row.
options.risk: The plate may not have enough width to pan; needs the still framed wide.
options.source: docs/flow/video-prompting.md §3 (frame the still for the move you will ask for)

recommended.why: Brief and clean; the stop after motion does the work and the waveform is the hero, as ruled.

frames.job: Establish where the hundred live: lived-in, human, five years hidden.

options.label: Locked tunnel, small life
options.idea: Locked frame; washing on the line stirs in a draught, steam rises from the kettle, one far figure crosses. The muffled argument grows louder down the tunnel.

lanes.does: Washing sways, kettle steam, one distant figure crosses with their back to us.
16mm grade, gate weave, grain.
The argument's sound rising across the shot.

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. A draught down the tunnel makes the hanging washing sway gently on its line; steam rises from the kettle on the trestle table; one person in a cardigan walks slowly away down the far end. Keep the 16mm grain and faded colour. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: hard cut from the waveform. Out: cut on the sound peak into the washroom (#6).
options.risk: Blast doors and a long corridor are hinge-able; any camera move will hinge them, so keep it locked.
options.source: docs/flow/video-prompting.md §9 (Veo hinges what is hinge-able); docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §2 step 2

options.label: Sound leads, still holds
options.idea: Post only. The still holds with 16mm gate weave while the argument, still muffled, gets closer; the sound is doing the travel.

lanes.does: Held plate.
16mm treatment, moving grain, gate weave.

options.cut: In: hard cut. Out: on the first clear word, cut to #6.
options.risk: If held too long it reads as a photo.
options.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §3 (J-cut); docs/story-craft/forms.md §2 (sound may lead picture)

options.label: Save it for #13
options.idea: Cut straight from the waveform to the washroom (#6) so the joke lands harder; use the tunnel later as the shot that the boom echoes down at #13.

lanes.does: Moved to #13.

options.cut: Out of this position entirely.
options.risk: Viewers may not know they are underground until #13; the washroom tiles and pipe may be enough.
options.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §4 step 5 (cut shots that repeat a job); docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/restructure-2026-10-15.md C2 (the juxtaposition is the joke)

recommended.why: One wide, once, with real life in it; the locked camera avoids the hinge problem with the doors.

frames.job: Reveal the signal's source: two people, full volume, about a toilet seat.

options.label: Locked wide, the row in gesture
options.idea: The pair keep arguing in big gestures, pointing at the seat; the flickering tube is added in post so its rhythm can be timed to the shouting.

lanes.does: Two people gesturing hard, no lip-sync needed at this size.
Strobe Light on the tube area or ffmpeg geq flicker, timed to the lines.
16mm grade, grain.

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. The man and the woman keep arguing by the sinks: she jabs a finger at the raised toilet seat, he throws his hands up and points back at her. Big angry gestures. Everything else stays still. Keep the 16mm grain. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: hard cut with the sound jump. Out: cut to the close two-shot #7 (wide to close).
options.risk: Hands may smear; two movers is safe.
options.source: docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/restructure-2026-10-15.md C2; docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §3 (force verbs: jab, throw); docs/google-flow/README.md (what the video model cannot do) (small text and timed effects go to post)

options.label: Smash cut on a still
options.idea: No motion: the full-volume row lands over the held still with a flicker in post. The sound jump is the whole effect.

lanes.does: Held plate.
Tube flicker via geq, grain.

options.cut: In: hard cut on the sound. Out: cut to #7.
options.risk: Next to moving clips a held still may read flat.
options.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §3 (a hard cut is never neutral); docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §2 table

options.label: She slams the seat
options.idea: Veo animates the woman slamming the seat down as the punctuation of her line.

lanes.does: One hand action: the seat goes down.

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. The woman reaches into the cubicle and slams the toilet seat down hard. The man flinches. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: hard cut. Out: on the slam, cut to #7.
options.risk: High: a hand using a prop and reaching a new state is on the cannot-do list.
options.source: docs/google-flow/README.md (what the video model cannot do)

recommended.why: Motion without asking the engine for a prop or a state change; flicker timed exactly in post.

frames.job: Spend the human-scale frame: the last humans on Earth, at full pettiness, close up.

options.label: One speaker per clip
options.idea: Two Veo clips from the new still, each favouring one face while the other is turned away. Cut between them like a real row. Voices from AI Studio.

lanes.does: Clip 1: the woman (cream jumper) talks and gestures, the man listens turned three-quarters away. Clip 2: the reverse.
Cut between the two on the line changes; dialogue laid from AI Studio voices.

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. The woman in the cream cable-knit jumper argues hard, jabbing a finger, her face angry; the man in the dark green jumper stands turned partly away, arms folded, shaking his head. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: from the wide #6. Out: the last line cuts to the red flip #8.
options.risk: These two are not Flow Characters, so mouths will not match our voice lines exactly; keep the listener's face away from camera.
options.source: docs/google-flow/README.md (what the video model cannot do) (two speakers in one clip; a line from a non-Character); docs/cinematography/principles.md R2 (the human-scale exception)

options.label: Silent gesture, words laid loose
options.idea: One clip, both gesture with mouths mostly hidden or turned; the dialogue runs loosely over it. The film is narrated, so tight sync is not needed.

lanes.does: Both gesture, no lip-sync asked.
Dialogue as L-cut from #6.

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. The two keep arguing in silence with big gestures: she points at something off-frame, he spreads his arms in disbelief, both shaking their heads. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: from #6. Out: to #8.
options.risk: Veo may add mouth movement anyway; at close range this can look like bad dubbing.
options.source: docs/story-craft/forms.md §2 (loose word-to-picture); docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §3 (L-cut)

options.label: One clip, two crops
options.idea: Generate one two-shot clip and cut two tighter punch-ins from it in Premiere for rhythm (wide, her, him).

lanes.does: One two-shot clip.
Two static crops of 140-160%.

options.veo_prompt: Same as option b.
options.cut: In: from #6. Out: to #8.
options.risk: Crops lose resolution (720p source); keep them under 1.6x.
options.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §5 (30-degree rule: change size, never nudge); docs/flow/video-prompting.md §3 (resolution)

recommended.why: The 15 Oct meeting ruled narration, not lip-sync: keep mouths mostly hidden and lay the row under it loosely. (Changed from A by Claude for that ruling.)

frames.job: Jeopardy: the machines commit and the colour flips to say so.

options.label: Veo rush, cut early
options.idea: Let Veo drive the camera hard down the street on the red plate; the motion blur and scan lines hide artefacts. Cut before the shopfronts start to regenerate.

lanes.does: Fast forward rush.
Single-frame flip from CCTV grey to red; KILL MODE ENGAGED; target brackets; photosensitivity pass.
Camera Shake high; trim to 2-3s.

options.veo_prompt: Racing fast forward down the ruined high street at knee height, the road rushing at camera, shopfronts streaking past in motion blur, debris flying. Keep the red monochrome image and scan lines.
options.cut: In: hard cut from the row on the last shouted word. Out: cut on the motion to the bot (#9).
options.risk: Rows of shopfronts regenerate after 3-4s; the red blur hides some of it.
options.source: memory: dramatic-video-animation (Kai, 2026-09-13); docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/scenes/second-half-storyboard-plan.md HUD rule; docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §2b

options.label: Post rush on the still
options.idea: No credit: a fast eased push plus directional blur on the red still, with heavy shake. The plate already has motion blur, so it reads as speed.

lanes.does: Scale ramp 100 to 140% over 2s, Directional Blur, Camera Shake.
Red flip, HUD, scanlines, photosensitivity.

options.cut: In: hard cut. Out: to #9.
options.risk: Without parallax it can read as a zoom on a picture.
options.source: docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §6c (the zoom-on-an-image complaint); docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §3 (make the move not read as a slideshow)

options.label: POV + corner CCTV
options.idea: Intercut the red POV with a grainy high corner camera of them rounding a bend (the unpicked K1-cctv still on the mood board), as the restructure describes.

lanes.does: K1: three machines race round the corner, debris kicked up.
Alternate red POV and corner CCTV, 1s each.
Both HUDs; timestamp on the CCTV.

options.veo_prompt: High corner security camera, the camera does not move. Three tracked machines race round the corner and away, debris and dust kicked up behind them. Keep the video noise and fisheye. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: hard cut. Out: to #9.
options.risk: Needs K1 approved as a still first; three fast movers can smear.
options.source: docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/restructure-2026-10-15.md beat D; docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/scenes/second-half-moodboard.md K1-cctv; docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §2 (a montage is a scene)

recommended.why: This is where the sequence spends its camera move; the red, noisy image is the best cover Veo will get.

frames.job: Tie the two threads: the machines rip past the bot we already love.

options.label: Spinning in the dust
options.idea: Locked low; the bot keeps spinning on the spot, beacon flashing, as the machines shrink away into their own dust.

lanes.does: Bot spins, machines recede, dust rolls.
16mm grade; beacon flash strengthened with geq if Veo's is weak.

options.veo_prompt: Low, the camera does not move. The small six-wheeled robot keeps spinning round on the spot in the wash of dust, its amber beacon flashing. Far down the road the three tracked machines keep racing away into their own dust cloud. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: on motion from #8. Out: the bot's line 'Boss, why are the kill bots going somewhere?' carries into #10.
options.risk: A spinning wheeled robot can change its shape mid-turn; ask for a slow spin.
options.source: docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/restructure-2026-10-15.md beat D (racing past the bot ties the threads); docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §2

options.label: Whip into the bot
options.idea: A whip pan in Premiere out of the red POV lands on the bot as the machines pass; it reads as one rush.

lanes.does: Whip pan with Directional Blur across the cut.
As option a.

options.veo_prompt: As option a.
options.cut: In: whip from #8. Out: to #10.
options.risk: A whip can feel showy if used twice; once only.
options.source: docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §3 (cut on movement)

options.label: Still + dust element
options.idea: Hold the still; a dust cloud made in Flow on black is keyed over, and the beacon flash is made in post.

lanes.does: The plate.
A rolling dust cloud element.
Luma Key the dust over the plate.

options.veo_prompt: A rolling cloud of grey dust blowing across from right to left on a pure black background. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: from #8. Out: to #10.
options.risk: Keyed dust can look pasted on; feather the edge.
options.source: docs/video-fx/README.md (the house answer for atmospherics)

recommended.why: It ties the threads in one shot and puts the bot's worry on screen before he speaks.

frames.job: Close the distance: they are heading for the mound where the humans are.

options.label: Veo tracking aerial
options.idea: Let Veo track alongside the three machines over the downs: open landscape, no grid, the kind of shot Veo handles well.

lanes.does: Lateral aerial tracking, dust trails.
Grade to dusk; trim.

options.veo_prompt: Aerial tracking shot moving alongside three tracked machines racing in a line across the rolling chalk downs, long trails of dust behind them, heading for a grassy mound with a concrete vent. Warm low sun.

frames.job: Back to the ordinary present: someone is watching this very film.

options.source: docs/stories/gitpush-origin-master/restructure-2026-10-15.md beat J; docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §4 (chained or reversed pull-out); docs/premiere/effects-catalogue.md (Corner Pin)

options.label: Push into the phone

Rain and lights.

options.label: Just the over-shoulder

recommended.why: It is the ruled ending (zoom out of a screen over someone's shoulder) and the cut-free join makes the regress felt.

frames.job: The button: the ordinary world goes on. 'Don't make me come back twice.'

options.source: docs/cinematography/frame.md §4 (an empty frame after a figure is punctuation); docs/flow/physics-and-motion.md §6b

frames.job: Break the row with the outside world: the noise stops, everyone turns.

options.label: Light floods, faces turn
options.idea: Locked tunnel. The doors swing open at the far end, daylight and smoke pour down the tunnel, the pair freeze mid-point and turn. The row cuts off on a hard sound stop.

lanes.does: Doors open, light and smoke roll in, the pair and the people behind turn to look.
Hard cut in from #13 on her raised finger; the row audio stops dead on the first door clang.

The woman in the cream jumper stops mid-point and turns to stare; the man beside her turns too; the people behind them stand up slowly. The camera does not move.
options.cut: In: hard cut from the row (#13). Out: to #15, the bot in the doorway.
options.risk: Many people turning at once: keep it to the pair plus background stillness if it smears.
options.source: docs/video-fx/hybrid-method.md §1 (camera locked); docs/cinematography/motion-and-cutting.md §3 (sound leads the cut)

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. The heavy green blast doors at the end of the tunnel swing open, a shaft of grey daylight and smoke rolling in. The camera does not move.

options.risk: Low.

options.label: Hold the still, push in
options.idea: No generation: the still held, a slow Premiere push towards the bright doorway, smoke added as a Flow element on black.

frames.job: The first contact: the smallest, friendliest thing walks in where they feared the worst.
